items.title: Park users will be relieved to hear about a new plan in Mississauga: city
items.summary: Mississauga is planning to put porta-potties in some of the city’s busiest parks after residents complained about a lack of washrooms in those areas. City of Mississauga staff will “investigate the feasibility of establishing a seasonal portable washroom pilot program … at select high-use city parks” following council’s approval on Tuesday of a motion calling for a Porta-Potties in Parks Pilot Program. Ward 4 Coun. John Kovac brought the motion forward, noting many residents have “expressed their dismay” over the years at not having convenient access to washrooms while enjoying many of the city’s parks. Kovac said only some of Mississauga’s larger green spaces offer bathroom facilities. “And what do we all think of when we want to go to a park and enjoy what our great parks have to offer? Amenities, shelters, seating and yet, for the most part, our parks do not have washroom facilities, being that it would be an extremely high expense,” he added. ” Kovac pointed to Ottawa, Toronto and Hamilton as cities that have “implemented something very similar” to the portable washroom plan he proposed. “This, potentially, could be one small step for council, but a giant relief for the public,” he added wryly, prior to council’s vote.

items.title: Road Closures Follow Fatal Hit-and-Run Involving Pickup Truck in Mississauga
items.summary: According to CBC Toronto and Insauga, a pedestrian died Tuesday evening after being hit by a pickup truck in a hit and run at Winston Churchill Boulevard and Dundas Street West in Mississauga. Peel Regional Police say the victim, an adult, was struck by the vehicle and pronounced dead at the scene, though officers have not released further details about who was killed. A spokesperson with Peel Regional Paramedic Services confirmed only that the victim was an adult. Police shut down all eastbound and westbound lanes on Dundas Street between Hampshire Gate and Woodchester Drive through the Winston Churchill intersection while investigators worked the scene. Drivers in the area faced significant delays, and police urged motorists to avoid the intersection while emergency crews remained on site. Peel Regional Police are asking anyone with information about the crash to call their non-emergency line at 905-453-3311.

items.title: From scenic trails to beach days: Discover Mississauga's must-visit waterfront spots
items.summary: Mississauga’s lakeshore along Lake Ontario’s northern shore features a large network of parks, trails, small beaches, green spaces and conservation areas all free to access. A pair of swans cruising along the shoreline of Jack Darling Memorial Park in Mississauga. Mississauga may often reside in the shadow of Toronto — its larger, more famous neighbour to the east — when it comes to recreational attractions, but the two cities share the same impressive waterfront on the northern shores of Lake Ontario. While you won’t find the kinds of beaches Toronto offers, Mississauga’s waterfront spans 22 kilometres between Toronto to the east and Oakville to the west, much of it accessible to the public via an extensive network of scenic parks, trails and conservation areas. If you’re looking for great picnic spots, walking and cycling trails, or maybe great food with a view, or an escape into nature from the urban hustle and bustle, here are four great spots to check out along Mississauga’s lakeshore. All parks, beaches and conservation areas listed below are public spaces and free to access. The Port Credit lighthouse located near the junction between the Credit River and Lake Ontario. No visit to Mississauga’s lakeshore is complete without a stop in scenic Port Credit.

items.title: Family of 19-year-old killed by Toronto police in Mississauga search for answers: 'Why did Kaleym not make it home?'
items.summary: The 19-year-old was shot and killed after five unmarked Toronto police vehicles tailed his car to a quiet Mississauga street, police watchdog says. Kaleym Davy was shot and killed by Toronto police in Mississauga on Aug. 6. Kaleym Davy’s grandmother says she wants answers about the night her 19-year-old grandson was shot dead on a quiet Mississauga cul-de-sac — and, so far, she hasn’t gotten any. Kaleym died in the early hours of Aug. 6 after five unmarked Toronto police vehicles tailed a white Mercedes sedan to Delfi Road, the province’s police watchdog said. The pursuit stemmed from a firearms investigation that began hours earlier in downtown Toronto. Marie Yee said her grandson was behind the wheel of the Mercedes, with three passengers in the vehicle, when he parked it near the home of a family member. “He was so close to his cousin’s house,” Yee said. Shortly after midnight, officers tried to stop the car, but the driver of the vehicle attempted to flee and struck one of the officers, according to the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), which is probing the fatal shooting. A collision between three unmarked police vehicles and the Mercedes then occurred, while an officer standing on the road fired through the driver’s side window, killing Kaleym, the SIU said. There was no evidence of an “exchange” of gunfire, SIU spokesperson Monica Hudon told reporters later that morning, but noted that two firearms were recovered near the Mercedes.

items.title: Council Approves Advisory Body to Track AI Data Centre Study and Report Back to Mississauga Residents
items.summary: According to Insauga, Mississauga city council voted Tuesday to create a Hyperscale Data Centre Task Force made up of councillors, city planning staff, industry stakeholders and members of the public. The temporary body is meant to keep residents informed as senior staff carry out a comprehensive review of large data centres and any new provincial rules that could regulate the fast growing industry. Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden brought forward the motion creating the task force, which is expected to provide regular updates and what the city calls transparent reporting for the public's benefit. The move comes two weeks after council unanimously approved an interim control bylaw imposing a one to two year moratorium on new large data centre developments in Mississauga. City officials say pausing new projects will give staff more time to study the issue and any regulations the province introduces before more facilities are approved.
